import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_17/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_17/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_17/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source0 and Source1 on movie_id to get title with ratings
df_0_1 = pd.merge(source0, source1[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='inner')

# Join the above result with Source2 on user_id to get gender info
df_all = pd.merge(df_0_1, source2[['user_id', 'gender']], on='user_id', how='inner')

# Group by title and calculate average rating filtered by gender
# For 'F' gender
f_ratings = df_all[df_all['gender'] == 'F'].groupby('title')['rating'].mean().rename('F')
# For 'M' gender
m_ratings = df_all[df_all['gender'] == 'M'].groupby('title')['rating'].mean().rename('M')

# Combine the two series into a DataFrame
result = pd.concat([f_ratings, m_ratings], axis=1).reset_index()

# Ensure columns have correct types: title (string), F (float), M (float)
result['title'] = result['title'].astype(str)
result['F'] = result['F'].astype(float)
result['M'] = result['M'].astype(float)

# Write the final target table to the specified path without the index
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_17/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_17/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_17/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_17/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_17_0 and Source3_17_1 on movie_id
join_0_1 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source3_17_2 on user_id
join_all = pd.merge(join_0_1, source2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Compute average rating grouped by title and gender
# Pivot the table to get separate columns for F and M average ratings
# First, filter ratings by gender and aggregate
grouped = join_all.groupby(['title', 'gender'])['rating'].mean().reset_index()

# Pivot to get columns 'F' and 'M'
pivot = grouped.pivot(index='title', columns='gender', values='rating').reset_index()

# Rename columns to match target schema
pivot = pivot.rename(columns={'F': 'F', 'M': 'M'})

# Ensure columns order as in target schema
pivot = pivot[['title', 'F', 'M']]

# Write output to the target file
pivot.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_17/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
